name: UX Layer
description: Models the user interface: views and screens, library components and their application-specific instances, forms, action and state patterns, component properties and the visual hierarchy they compose (HTML 5.3 vocabulary with component-library conventions). Rendered components, templates and view classes are evidence for elements here; the logic they call belongs to the application layer and the paths that reach them to the navigation layer. Modelling rules: placement is composition. A view composes its sub-views, component instances and action components; a sub-view or library sub-view composes its instances; an instance composes its nested instances, action components, slot references, chart series and table columns, and a menu composes its entries. A UX library aggregates its library components and sub-views, and a library component composes the components and slot references it is built from; an instance or placed sub-view realizes the library definition it places, and a slot reference references the component that fills it. Elements apply their layout configuration; state transitions, state patterns and action patterns use transition templates, which describe motion only. A state pattern aggregates its states; a state composes its outgoing transitions, a transition flows to its destination state, states and transitions trigger state actions, and a state action realizes its template. An action pattern governs the action components it is applied to. A view, sub-view, component instance or action component binds to its data configuration, which maps to the API or data-model data it reads; chart series and table columns bind through their component. Elements use their error configuration. A view realizes the application interface it presents and the product feature it delivers; an action component triggers the API operation or application behaviour it starts. UX does not access stores, operations or services directly, and reaches the business layer through the application interfaces and features it realizes: a view serves the business role it is for and references the business object it shows. A view supports the goals and outcomes it contributes to, and UX elements satisfy requirements and principles.
